dynarules 0.2.0 — visualisation review

917 events → 200 transactions, 170 co-occurrence rules, 30 sequential rules.

Network views are drawn by cograph (splot()), not by dynarules. The other five views are ggplot2.

Whether a network is directed depends on the weight: confidence, conviction and laplace are asymmetric and give directed graphs; lift, support, kappa, jaccard, cosine, phi and leverage are symmetric and give undirected ones. Sequential rules are always directed.

Co-occurrence rules

1. scatter — the default

Support against confidence, coloured by lift. Diverging palette centred on lift = 1, so blue beats independence and red falls short of it.

2. two-key

The same scatter, coloured by rule order instead. Shows how the longer rules concentrate at low support.

3. matrix

Antecedent against consequent, tiled by the chosen measure.

4. grouped

Antecedents collapsed to their lead item; point size is support. (arulesViz clusters antecedents here — this groups them deterministically instead, so no clustering dependency is needed.)

5. graph

Handed to cograph::splot(). as_network() already emits a cograph_network, so dynarules does not draw networks itself — it passes the object to the house renderer. Anything splot() accepts (layout, node and edge styling) passes straight through the ....

Directedness is derived, not assumed. The default weight is lift, which is symmetric for co-occurrence rules — lift(a→b) equals lift(b→a) — so the network above is drawn undirected. Weighting by confidence, which is asymmetric, gives a genuinely directed network:

6. paracoord

Each rule is a path across item positions; the last position is the consequent.

Sequential rules

The same views over order-aware rules. Note the axis labels switch to the -> separator and the title reports “Sequential”.
